guidance.schedule: Two sessions a week, ideally 2–3 days apart. Day 1 and Day 2 are session labels; train on the days that suit you. Allow around 65–80 minutes including warm-up.
guidance.warmup: Start with 5 minutes of easy movement. Do 2–3 progressively heavier warm-up sets for your first press and pull, plus a light rehearsal of your first leg exercise. Warm-up sets do not count toward the totals.
guidance.progression: Keep compound lifts for each four-week block. When every working set reaches the top of its rep range with the target reps in reserve, add the smallest available load next time (usually 2–5%). Otherwise add a rep or repeat the load. Compare matching exercises, not different variations.
guidance.effort: RIR means reps in reserve: how many clean reps you could still do. Most work stops with 2–3 reps left. No forced reps or failure targets. Use a comfortable range and swap an exercise if it causes pain.
guidance.variety: New compound combinations every four weeks. Week 2 of each block rotates finishers; week 3 returns to the original finishers with a lower rep range on the first two lifts. Weeks 4, 8 and 12 reduce volume and effort.
guidance.balance: Regular sessions: 16 upper + 4 lower working sets = 80/20 by direct programmed sets. Recovery sessions: 10 upper + 2 lower sets. Compound exercises also involve other muscles, so this is an emphasis rather than a physiological percentage.
guidance.goal: Build and maintain muscle with repeatable strength work. Visible definition also depends on nutrition and body-fat levels; this cycle does not promise spot fat loss.
guidance.core: Optional: after either session add 2 easy sets of dead bugs or Pallof presses if time allows. These are extra core work and excluded from the 80/20 working-set count.
guidance.cycle: After week 12, review your logged loads and choose a new cycle. The app holds at week 12 rather than silently looping.
